sources.entry: move_pages(2) - Defines per-page migration of a running process, and a query reporting each page's node, the direct test of first touch.

summary.title: move_pages(2) — Linux manual page
summary.one_liner: move_pages(2) explains how to move individual pages of a running process to a chosen NUMA node, or query which node each page currently resides on.
takeaways: move_pages(pid, count, pages, nodes, status, flags) moves listed pages of a process to target NUMA nodes.
Passing nodes as NULL makes move_pages() report the node each page currently resides on in the status array, which is useful for checking placement.
Status values include node numbers and errors such as -EACCES, -EBUSY, -ENOENT and -ENOMEM.
MPOL_MF_MOVE moves only exclusively used pages; MPOL_MF_MOVE_ALL also moves shared pages but needs CAP_SYS_NICE.
Since Linux 4.13, moving pages of another process is governed by a PTRACE_MODE_READ_REALCREDS check.
summary.summary: This is the Linux man-pages reference page for the move_pages(2) system call, covering its signature, arguments, flags, and permission rules. It describes the two uses of the call: moving specified pages to target NUMA nodes, and querying each page's current node by passing a NULL nodes array. The page also lists per-page status codes, return values and errors, and notes on cpuset and memory policy interaction. It is a reference rather than a tutorial, and the listing frames it as a direct way to test first-touch placement.
